mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, or the average 20d return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals tight labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain or raise rates, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20d returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE < 3.5%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits above 1.1 million units signals strong household demand and rising inflationary pressures, which triggers a hawkish monetary policy response and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1100.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 108.0 index points signals weakening manufacturing activity and a contraction in real output, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60d returns in more than 60% of cases when INDPRO < 108.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong aggregate demand and rising inflation expectations, which triggers a hawkish monetary policy response and suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances where both RSAFS and HOUST are rising, or the joint signal fails to produce a significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPI inflation rate above 2.5% combined with a stable federal funds rate signals that inflation is outpacing monetary policy response, increasing real interest rate uncertainty and reducing equity risk appetite, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS <= 2.5%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200k per month combined with a declining unemployment rate signals a labor market overheating, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 200.0 and UNRATE < 3.7%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP growth above 2.0% annualized combined with rising residential construction permits signals strong economic momentum and rising inflation expectations, which triggers a hawkish monetary policy response and suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60d returns in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 > 18900.0 and HOUST > 1100.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
